cards.note: Wild sunflowers (Verbesina encelioides) are often found in Salta, Jujuy and Tucumán.
Along the border with Uruguay in Entre Rios and Corrientes is where you'll most commonly find tree plantations in Argentina. There may be others rarely in other parts of these provinces/Argentina.

Bariloche is a famous resort town in Nuequen. It can be recognized by the ski town vibes, the lake, and the mountains. While there are some other similar towns in Southern Argentina, Bariloche stands out and can be recognized with practice!
Just north of Buenos Aires City near Villa Paranacito there is boat coverage that is recognizable with the foliage and sometimes visible architecture.

cards.a: Buenos Aires Black and Yellow Taxi
cards.note: Black taxis with yellow rooftops can be seen commonly in the capital of Buenos Aires. While they should be unique to Buenos Aires Similar but distint taxis can be found in other cities.
Small ponds near the road are occasionally seen in the province of Buenos Aires.

Trichocereus atacamensis, or the cardón, is a cactus native to the high elevation mountain ranges of Catamarca, Tucumán, Salta and Jujuy. It can be identified by its candelabra-like appearance and fuzzy golden brown spines.
In the Chaco and Formosa provinces, you will often see sandy soil with an abundance of vegetation; mainly low trees and bushes.
Comodoro Rivadavia is built on the slopes of Chenque hill, making the city recognisable.
Taxis in Cordoba are often all yellow or all green. May be seen uncommonly in other towns but if you're in a very large city with similar taxis it's likely Cordoba.
Snow coverage is found on the eastern RP25 in eastern Santa Cruz.
Semi-coastal grass hills are seen in southern Buenos Aires, especially northeast of Bahía Blanca.
The northern province of Jujuy has unique architecture similar to that of the brick buildings in Bolivia and Peru.

T-Junctions in La Pampa sometimes have these usually yellow (rarely other colors) rectangular signs, with a chevron pattern on the bottom, usually the Road Number(s) above, with an arrow on both sides.
Within Argentina, these Latvian style wooden hook poles are unique to La Rioja and Mendoza. (A bit more common in La Rioja, which also has a drier, more desert-like feel)
The soil in misiones is a distinct red color (similar to the Brazil across the border). This combined with the vegetation in the area can be a good clue for this region.

The monkey puzzle tree can be found in western Neuquen. The most specimens are seen on state road 23.

NOTE: They are seen on the other side in Chile as well.
Pampas grass (Cortaderia selloana) is one of the most defining flora of the Pampas region. It is recognizable by its long bunched reeds and white fluffy flowerheads.
The Pink Trumpet Tree (Handroanthus impetiginosus) can be found in cities in northern Salta such as Orán, Tartagal, General Mosconi and Salvador Mazza.
Sunset coverage with degraded image quality is found on the RN40 just south of the Mendoza border with Neuquén.
These red mountains are unique to the RN68 valley in southern Salta.
Roads with reddish pavement lined with long Argentine needle-grass are common in San Luis.
The “sawdust” car is found in centre-south Argentina (mostly west Rio Negro) and has a unique sandy dust on its visible black back.
If you see this kind of vegetation with flat grass and a low number of bushes, you are almost certainly in the state of Tierra del Fuego or southeastern Santa Cruz.
Sugarcane plantations are most common in Tucumán, with hotspots appearing in Salta and Jujuy.
Prosopis caldenia, known as the caldén, is a decently large deciduous tree with small leaves and sinuous branches. It is mainly found in La Pampa.

Stetsonia coryne, or the toothpick cactus, is a large tree-like cactus with many branches and spines resembling toothpicks. Its habitat includes a hotspot between Catamarca and Cordoba as well as the border area between Chaco, Salta and Formosa.
White vertical pole stickers with several digits can be found in Tucumán.
The southernmost city of Argentina, Ushuaia, is easily recognizable by the snowy mountains to the north, the archictecture, and the vegetation.
Well forested mountainous areas around Ushuaia in Southern Tierra Del Fuego are easily recognized.
Unusually wide dirt roads and flat geography make the Valdes peninsula of Eastern Chubut recognizable.
Villa Dique Florentino Ameghino in northeastern Chubut is surrounded by these rock formations.
